core_obligations: Work on one good object and compute the chain (proof lines 16628-16652): for an etale U -> X whose structure morphism factors as U -> V -> S with V -> S etale and U -> V quasi-compact with geometrically connected fibres (hence flat), the five terms f^{-1}g_*F(U) = g_*F(V) = F(V x_S T) = e^{-1}F(U x_X Y) = h_*e^{-1}F(U) are identified one by one: the first by sections upstairs together with locality of pullback along U -> V, the second by the definition of g_*, the third by sections upstairs applied to U x_X Y -> V x_S T, whose fibres are geometrically connected as a base change, and the fourth by the definition of h_*.
Note the identification U x_X Y = U x_S T (proof line 16647): this follows from Y = X x_S T and is what makes the third step applicable.
Conclude by locality (proof lines 16654-16661): by hypothesis every object of X_etale admits an etale covering to which the computation applies, so the two sheaves agree locally, hence globally.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to an object U of X_etale with the factorisation U -> V -> S and quasi-compact geometrically connected fibres.
Identify the five terms of the displayed chain using sections upstairs, the definition of the pushforwards, and the base change of geometric connectedness.
Spread over a covering to obtain the identity f^{-1}g_*F = h_*e^{-1}F of sheaves of sets.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is a base change statement for pushforwards of sheaves of sets along a flat morphism whose etale objects admit local factorisations with quasi-compact geometrically connected fibres (statement lines 16609-16625). The proof (proof lines 16627-16661) is a five-term computation of sections on one good object, using sections upstairs twice (once for U -> V, once for U x_X Y -> V x_S T, whose fibres are geometrically connected by base change), the identification U x_X Y = U x_S T, and the definitions of the two pushforwards, followed by localisation over a covering. H2: one explicit section computation followed by a locality argument.
